study_identification.title: Comprehensive volumetric phenotyping of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome

study_characteristics.study_objective: To conduct the first comprehensive volumetric phenotyping of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome (DS) using normative modeling, and to assess the impact of congenital heart defects (CHD) on brain volumes.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Exclusion criteria included incidental findings on MRI with possible or likely significance for clinical outcome and/or imaging analysis, including acute infarction or parenchymal hemorrhage, and major lesions within the WM, cortical GM, cerebellum, or basal ganglia. We did not exclude neonates with < 10 punctate white matter lesions (PWML), small subependymal cysts, small subdural hemorrhages, or hemorrhages in the caudothalamic notch. Bayley III Scales of Infant Development (BSIDIII) cognitive and motor composite scores below 70 at 18 months.

response_variable.answer: Absolute and relative tissue volumes for 7 main tissue/fluid classes and further segmented specific tissue segments.

predictor_variables.answer: Sex; PMA at scan (in weeks); age from birth (in weeks)

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper does not mention any specific methods to handle nuisance structures like site effects, scanner differences, or other potential confounders beyond the specified predictors.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: The paper states that the normative model accounted for sex, PMA at scan, and age from birth variables. There is no mention of other nuisance variables.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not describe any validation of the normative model on a non-independent subset of the training data.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The paper describes the application of the trained model to the Down syndrome cohort, but not a validation on a hold-out set from the dHCP cohort.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not describe any validation of the normative model on an independent dataset from the same domain.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: The paper applies the model to a clinical sample (Down syndrome) but does not validate it on an independent healthy control sample.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not describe any validation of the normative model on a dataset from a different domain.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: The study focuses on the application of the model to the Down syndrome cohort, not on external validation.

clinical_dataset.answer: Early Brain Imaging in DS (eBiDS) study

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Mann-Whitney U test and Kruskal-Wallis one-way test of variance were used to test statistical difference between groups (DS vs control, DS with CHD vs without CHD). Simple linear regressions were used to model the relationship between volumetric z-scores and PMA at scan, and volumetric z-scores and whole brain volume z-scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The neonatal brain in DS is characterized by significantly reduced whole brain, cerebral white matter, and cerebellar volumes; reduced relative frontal and occipital lobar volumes, in contrast with enlarged relative temporal and parietal lobar volumes; enlarged relative deep gray matter volume; and enlargement of the lateral ventricles.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Neonates with DS showed significantly smaller absolute whole brain volumes. Relative volumes revealed altered tissue proportionality, with enlarged temporal and parietal lobes and reduced frontal and occipital lobes. Deep gray matter, particularly the lentiform nuclei, was proportionally enlarged. The cerebellum was disproportionately small. The presence of congenital heart defects (CHD) was associated with more pronounced volumetric reductions, particularly in the occipital white matter.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The primary limitation was the small sample size of neonates with DS, especially for subgroup analyses (e.g., CHD+ vs CHD-). The study was cross-sectional, lacking longitudinal follow-up. Some brain structures were not automatically segmented. The study relied on structural MRI, without information on microstructure or neurocircuitry.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The ability to assess phenotypic severity at the neonatal stage may help guide early interventions and, ultimately, help improve neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with DS.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a comprehensive volumetric analysis of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome, highlighting the complex pattern of brain alterations present at birth and the potential impact of comorbidities like CHD.
